page: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v6 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by an Azure-tailored Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance supplies 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing deterministic execution across all 64 vCPUs. The CPU architecture includes a 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration with AES instructions.

System memory consists of 128 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2 GB per core. Benchmarks reveal exceptional memory subsystem capabilities, reaching 465.57 GB/s in large-block uncached read tests and 203.79 GB/s in large-block write operations, both ranking in the top 10% of evaluated systems. Additionally, the instance incorporates 3,780 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage, eliminating standard external volume latency for scratch and data caching operations. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data displays a pronounced contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded CPU throughput. Single-core tests such as Geekbench (1,697.0) and stress-ng (2,075.09) exhibit middle-tier results. Conversely, aggregate parallel throughput ranks in the top tier, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,430.0, a Clang compilation score of 65,496.0, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 600.8 GB/s. PassMark database operations also attained top-tier metrics at 37,402.55, supplemented by Redis throughput reaching 117.69 million set operations per second.

The 2 GB per core allocation makes this server less suited for large in-memory datasets or hyper-dense virtualization layers. However, the density of physical cores combined with high memory bandwidth and local NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for multi-threaded build systems, CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration nodes, web serving fleets, and high-throughput transactional database workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v6 provides 64 dedicated ARM-based Neoverse-N2 cores at 3.4 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It features 128 GB of system memory, providing a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The memory subsystem demonstrates top-tier performance, achieving 465.57 GB/s uncached read bandwidth and 203.79 GB/s write bandwidth. Multi-core compute performance is notably strong, as demonstrated by top-tier results in Clang software compilation, PassMark database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tests. Single-core throughput ranks within the mid-tier. The bundled high-speed local storage and core density yield high computational efficiency for parallelized processing tasks, making the instance an effective platform for software compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, batch processing workloads, and transactional database services requiring fast local caching.
